data.exact_reserve_text: The improved market conditions were offset by a number of factors such as deterioration of prior year reserves, increase in natural catastrophe loss activity in 2020 and the COVID-19 pandemic. With legacy year reserves continuing to be under pressure in many markets, an unprecedented number of natural catastrophes in 2020 and the COVID-19 pandemic all of these are having a positive impact on the future market conditions for both insurance and reinsurance lines. During the year, the exposure to Typhoon Hagibis has deteriorated on a gross basis, but net exposure is not material. The Syndicate also has material exposure to COVID-19 on the 2019 Year of Account.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross strengthening of prior year reserves by GBP 0.495 million, primarily driven by adverse claims development. This strengthening is observed in the 2018 underwriting year. The report also notes general deterioration of prior year reserves and specific adverse development related to Typhoon Hagibis and material exposure to COVID-19 for the 2019 Year of Account, although these specific impacts are not quantified separately from the overall prior year movement.
